cover_options.text: Anthropic now gives vetted security teams fewer cyber blocks on its newest Claude models
Anthropic merges Glasswing into a three-tier program easing cyber blocks for vetted teams
Anthropic folds Project Glasswing into a wider Cyber Verification Program with three tiers

body.text: For six months Anthropic ran Project Glasswing, Claude Mythos access for organizations securing the most critical software, and the CVP, for vetted security teams. The new program merges them.

headline.text: Public Claude models block most cyber work

body.text: Anthropic says cybersecurity is dual use, so Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Sonnet 5.5 have conservative safeguards. Code review, patching known issues and alert triage still work. Who gets fewer blocks?

Defense Access covers incident response and malware reverse-engineering; Anthropic aims to respond in a few days. Red Team adds authorized pen testing after a few weeks of review; blocks stay on ransomware.

headline.text: Fewest blocks go to orgs reviewed with the US government

body.text: Specialized Access is for a limited set of organizations testing power grids, telecom networks and interbank transfers. Glasswing members move in without reapproval for current models.

headline.text: Anthropic's test: Defense blocks most, Red Team none

body.text: Anthropic says Red Team Access matched the 67.6% success rate Opus 5.5 reaches with no safeguards. Without CVP access, every task was blocked on the first prompt.

headline.text: Anthropic's case for wider access: verified bugs

body.text: Anthropic says partners found them from April to July 2026, and its own open-source scanning added 5,500 more. More than 33,000 verified ones are rated critical or high severity so far.

headline.text: Anthropic says its own count is partial

body.text: It rests on 33 partner reports, and fewer than half of partners disclosed patched numbers. Anthropic expects true impact at least five times higher. No outside check of the figures or test results was found.

headline.text: Entry requires letting Anthropic retain data

body.text: Members must allow data retention so Anthropic can monitor for cyber misuse. Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, due later this fall, will let eligible organizations store data in cloud infrastructure they control.

caption.text:
Anthropic has merged Project Glasswing into an expanded Cyber Verification Program that gives vetted security teams fewer cyber blocks on its newest Claude models.

The program now has three tiers: Defense Access, Red Team Access and Specialized Access. Each includes Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Mythos 5.1. Anthropic says its public models block most cyber work because cybersecurity is dual use, meaning the same skills can help defenders or attackers. Specialized Access has the fewest blocks and is limited to verified organizations reviewed in depth with the US government.

Anthropic says Glasswing partners found at least 129,000 verified software vulnerabilities between April and July 2026, and uses that to justify wider access. It also says the figures are likely an undercount. No outside check of the numbers or of its CyScenarioBench test results was found. Members must also allow data retention so Anthropic can monitor for misuse.

Would you trust a company to decide who gets the most capable AI for security work?

Follow Helios for the next update on how Anthropic's cyber access plays out.
